title: feat(plugin): add the Agent Plugins mcp.json loader
body:
HUMAN: This PR loads MCP servers from an Agent Plugins package's mcp.json and registers the Agent Plugins format, keeping plugin servers away from the user's secrets. --- AGENT: ## Why An Agent Plugins package declares its MCP servers in `mcp.json` at the plugin root. We only read `.mcp.json`, so those servers were invisible — and `AgentPluginsFormat` was deliberately held out of the format registry until this landed (#4474), which meant a conformant package still loaded as a Claude Code plugin under a name inferred from its directory. The portable format is not a rename of ours. It defines exactly two placeholders and forbids every other kind of expansion, a containment boundary for package paths, remote URL and header rules, and a failure boundary per entry. Mapping it onto `MCPServer` is where that work lives. ## Summary - Adds `agent_plugins_mcp`, the `mcp.json` loader: vendored `mcp-1.0.0.schema.json`, top-level document validated closed, each entry validated independently against the `#/$defs/server` the spec exposes for exactly that purpose. An invalid document disables MCP for the plugin; an invalid or unsupported entry skips only itself. - Implements `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${PLUGIN_DATA}` in `args`, `env` values and `cwd` — single-pass, non-recursive, nothing else expanded — plus command resolution, `cwd` containment, remote URL and header validation. Headers the client generates (`Host`, `Content-Length`, `Mcp-Session-Id`, …) win over configured ones, and configured headers never follow a redirect to another origin. - Defines `PLUGIN_DATA` as `get_cache_path()` under `~/.openhands/plugin-data/` — `-`, the fetch cache's naming: outside `plugins/`, which is scanned for plugins; keyed by plugin root, which is already stable across updates, so each plugin instance keeps its own data and a same-named plugin elsewhere cannot share it. - A loader-only `MCPServer.as_literal()` exempts package servers from every `${VAR}` expansion site — now one helper, `expand_mcp_servers` — so a package cannot pull a user's secret or environment into its own subprocess. The flag is a private attribute: input cannot set it and dumps never write it. Plugin `env` and `headers` stay redacted like any other secret. - Registers `AgentPluginsFormat` ahead of the Claude Code fallback, the flip `test_not_registered_yet` was pinning. ## Issue Number Closes #4451. Part of #4405. ## How to Test End-to-end against the official example package plus the specification's own `mcp.json` example, both verbatim: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-example /tmp/ap-example mkdir -p /tmp/ap-example/bin && touch /tmp/ap-example/bin/validator cat > /tmp/ap-example/mcp.json <<'JSON' { "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json", "mcpServers": { "local-validator": { "type": "stdio", "command": "./bin/validator", "args": ["--data", "${PLUGIN_DATA}/validator"], "env": { "CONFIG": "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json" }, "cwd": "${PLUGIN_ROOT}" }, "deployment-api": { "type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://deploy.example.com/mcp", "headers": { "X-Tenant": "public-tenant" } }, "legacy-events": { "type": "sse", "url": "https://legacy.example.com/sse" } } } JSON uv run python -c " from pathlib import Path from openhands.sdk.mcp.config import dump_mcp_config from openhands.sdk.plugin import Plugin, detect_format root = Path('/tmp/ap-example') print('format :', detect_format(root).name) servers = Plugin.load(root).mcp_config for name, config in dump_mcp_config(servers).items(): print(name, config) print('redacted dump:', servers['deployment-api'].model_dump(mode='json')['headers'])" ``` This branch (`OH_PERSISTENCE_DIR=/tmp/oh-demo`): ``` format : agent-plugins local-validator {'transport': 'stdio', 'command': '/private/tmp/ap-example/bin/validator', 'args': ['--data', '/tmp/oh-demo/plugin-data/ap-example-6153411fe0a97c28/validator'], 'env': {'CONFIG': '/private/tmp/ap-example/config.json', 'PLUGIN_ROOT': '/private/tmp/ap-example', 'PLUGIN_DATA': '/tmp/oh-demo/plugin-data/ap-example-6153411fe0a97c28'}, 'cwd': '/private/tmp/ap-example'} deployment-api {'url': 'https://deploy.example.com/mcp', 'transport': 'streamable-http', 'headers': {'X-Tenant': 'public-tenant'}} redacted dump: {'X-Tenant': '**********'} ``` Line-wrapped for readability. `dump_mcp_config` is what the connection path uses; an ordinary dump redacts. `legacy-events` (`sse`) is reported and skipped; see Notes. On `main` the same package prints `claude-code`, loads as `ap-example` — the directory name — and has no MCP servers at all. **Tests.** ``` uv run pytest tests/sdk -q # 9 failed, 6347 passed (branch) uv run pytest tests/sdk -q # 9 failed, 6197 passed (22c85eb, same 9) uv run pytest tests/sdk/plugin tests/sdk/mcp tests/sdk/test_settings.py \ tests/sdk/conversation tests/cross/test_check_sdk_api_breakage.py -q uv run pre-commit run --files # all hooks pass uv run python .github/scripts/check_persisted_settings_compat.py # 14 fixtures, 8 baselines ``` Both suite runs use an empty `OH_PERSISTENCE_DIR`; the 9 failures are identical on both sides and are that override's doing — they assert the default `~/.openhands` path. The delta against `main` is zero. 86 tests cover the document, entry isolation, stdio, remote, serialization, `PLUGIN_DATA` and expansion. Two run over real transports: one launches a stdio server from a package and checks the cwd, argv and environment it got; one sends a request through a same-origin and then a cross-origin redirect between local HTTP servers and checks which headers arrived where. `TestAgentPluginsMCPExpansion` covers `_ensure_plugins_loaded` and `load_plugin()`. Each regression test was checked by reverting its fix, and every one fails without it. ## Video/Screenshots N/A — library change, no UI. The terminal output above is the evidence. ## Design Doc N/A. The design follows the specification section by section; decisions that were open questions on #4405 are in Notes. ## Type - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Docs / chore ## Notes **Three of #4405's open questions are answered here**, and each is cheap to revisit: 1. **`sse` is not supported** (question 1). It is OPTIONAL in the spec and deprecated by MCP itself; an `sse` entry is reported and skipped, which is a conformant outcome (§7.2.2 rule 4). Adding it later is one entry in `SUPPORTED_TRANSPORTS`; withdrawing it would not be. 2. **`PLUGIN_DATA` is `~/.openhands/plugin-data/-`** (question 5), built by the fetch cache's own `get_cache_path` and created only for a usable stdio server. Keyed by root, not manifest name: project plugins load ambiently and the spec puts `node_modules` and virtualenvs here, so name keying would let a repo ship a same-named plugin and plant code a trusted installed plugin then runs. Roots are already stable across updates (`installed/`, a source-hashed fetch cache path, fixed project paths), so the data survives one. It sits outside `plugins/`, whose every child is loaded as a plugin, and is not deleted on uninstall — a `MAY` left for a follow-up. 3. **Plugin `headers` and `env`: exempt from expansion, still redacted** (question 6). The spec calls header values "visible package data, not a portable secret mechanism"; that forbids plugins from putting secrets there but does not require clients to display them, so redaction protects the user from a plugin that does it anyway. Plugin servers are rebuilt from the package on every load, so no stored plaintext is needed. The expansion exemption is the part §9.2 requires. **Changes outside the plugin package.** Four call sites expanded `${VAR}` against the environment and per-conversation secrets with the same dump→expand→coerce block: `load_plugins()`, `_ensure_plugins_loaded`, and two in `LocalConversation.load_plugin()`. They now share `expand_mcp_servers()`, which leaves package servers alone; behavior for every other server is unchanged. In `mcp/utils.py`, package remote servers get an HTTP client whose request hook runs on every redirect hop and drops the configured header names once a request leaves the configured origin. FastMCP follows redirects and httpx strips only `Authorization`, so before this a `307` carried `X-Tenant` to a different origin; same-origin redirects still keep the headers. User-configured servers are unchanged and still have that httpx behavior, which is out of scope here. **Not in scope.** Path containment here covers what §7.2.1 makes part of entry validity — `command` and `cwd`. The general rule for every other package path is #4453. **Worth a reviewer's eye:** the top-level schema is derived from the vendored document by dropping `$defs` and loosening `mcpServers`, rather than restated, so the closed field set cannot drift — but it does mean the per-entry `$ref` is resolved from a second, hand-built validator. ---
